Solar panels use photovoltaic cells, usually made from silicon semiconductors, to convert light energy directly into electrical energy. Sunlight consists of photons, and when suitable photons are absorbed by the cell, they transfer energy to electrons, freeing them to move and creating an electric current. The cell’s p-type and n-type semiconductor layers create an electric field that directs this electron movement through an external circuit, producing direct-current (DC) electricity. Many cells are connected into a panel to increase the power output, and an inverter converts the panel’s DC electricity into alternating current (AC) for ordinary household use.

Solar panels use photovoltaic cells, usually made from silicon semiconductors, to convert light energy directly into electrical energy. [shard_06097_61882]

Sunlight consists of photons, and when suitable photons are absorbed by the cell, they transfer energy to electrons, freeing them to move and creating an electric current. [shard_00135_41357] [shard_06097_61882]

The cell’s p-type and n-type semiconductor layers create an electric field that directs this electron movement through an external circuit, producing direct-current (DC) electricity. [shard_06097_61882]
